description: baseline

Create a CUTE DSL hybrid dispatcher that detects small n=32/176/352 and upper-triangular or rank-deficient easy structures, using custom fast specialized kernels there and falling back only for unsupported hard cases after profiling baseline launch overhead.
CUDA extension upper-triangular fast path failed at import because torch load_inline could not find ninja in the build environment.
Added ninja PATH discovery, but the extension still failed because load_inline generated duplicate bindings and the CUDA source missed ATen CUDA stream declarations.
Extension builds after fixing bindings and includes, but validation guard rejects explicit CUDA stream usage in the kernel launch.
Upper-triangular detector now builds and validates; benchmark regressed to 117178.061 us because dense small shapes pay an extra detector launch and host sync before falling back.
Added a single-block custom Householder QR for n=32 and stopped probing n=176/352 dense cases; benchmark improved to 110321.014 us, mainly by cutting the n=32 shape from ~307 us to ~144 us.
Kept the custom n=32 QR path but disabled n=4096 upper-triangular probing on dense benchmark inputs; benchmark improved to 108982.073 us.

Added a n=512 rank-deficient detector that factors only the first 384 columns when the trailing 128 columns are exactly zero; benchmark improved to 106499.322 us, with the rankdef shape dropping from ~949 ms to ~752 ms despite detector overhead on dense/mixed n=512.

Best score reached 106499.322 us at 98af4b7bbb9afc7951c0f1903598c605b60a6354, down from baseline 115658.564 us. Useful changes were a custom single-block n=32 Householder QR kernel and a n=512 rank-deficient dispatcher that detects exactly-zero trailing 128 columns and factors only the first 384 columns; broad upper-triangular probing and dense small-shape detection were net negative due extra launches/syncs. CUTE DSL was unavailable in this environment (no cutlass module), so the viable custom path used torch load_inline CUDA; next briefs could target n=176/352 custom QR or lower-overhead rankdef detection/fusion.

Extend 98af4b with a dense medium-size CUDA QR fast path for n=176 first, using one matrix per CTA or panel-tiled Householder to reduce torch.geqrf overhead; try n=352 only after n=176 validates, preserve existing n=32 and n=512 rankdef wins, and dispatch by shape only with no broad dense/upper detection launches.
Tried a one-CTA n=176 Householder QR storing the full matrix in shared memory, but ptxas rejected it for 0x1e800 bytes shared memory above the 0xc000 limit.

Reworked n=176 one-CTA Householder QR to store the matrix in output global memory with only reduction scratch in shared memory; validates and improves benchmark to 103406.806 us, cutting n=176 from ~15.2 ms to ~10.9 ms.
Added a n=352 global-memory Householder QR after n=176 validated, but it regressed benchmark to 110397.742 us because n=352 rose to ~80 ms versus torch.geqrf ~38 ms.

Reverted the n=352 regression and restored the n=176-only custom QR candidate; validation passed and benchmark measured 103879.382 us (run noise above the earlier 103406.806 but still faster than parent).

Best score reached 103406.806 us at 2c0f05b2656749db814c8f6960c1c4fc8f411529, improving parent 106499.322 us. The winning change is a n=176 one-CTA Householder QR that keeps matrix state in output global memory and uses shared memory only for reductions; full shared-memory n=176 exceeded hardware shared-memory limits. A follow-up n=352 version validated but regressed badly (~80 ms vs torch.geqrf ~38 ms), so it was reverted; final branch head d73c01fc1e12fc55cc9c7693530a5ea291c7f4f2 preserves n=32, n=176, and n=512 rankdef wins. CUTE DSL remains unavailable, so implemented executable custom CUDA via load_inline.

Profile and micro-tune the existing n=176 one-CTA Householder QR path from 2c0f05 without changing dispatch: first reduce per-column global traffic or shared-reduction synchronization based on ncu/nsys evidence, then sweep only the smallest needed block/unroll/register knobs; preserve n=32 and n=512 rankdef paths and do not retry n=352 unless n=176 improves.
Replaced shared-memory tree reductions in the n=176 QR kernel with warp-shuffle block reductions; validation passed and benchmark improved to 100110.909 us, cutting n=176 from ~10.9 ms to ~7.2 ms.
Swept n=176 block size down to 128 threads with a four-warp block reduction; validation passed but benchmark regressed to 101402.890 us versus the 256-thread warp-reduction result.
Reverted the 128-thread sweep and restored the 256-thread warp-reduction QR176 kernel; validation passed and benchmark measured 100060.115 us, consistent with the best warp-reduction result.

Best score reached 100060.115 us at 367767a89abb701dfd75af80a15f4cadb780fa6a, improving parent 103406.806 us. The winning micro-tune replaced per-column shared-memory tree reductions in the n=176 QR kernel with warp-shuffle block reductions; n=176 dropped from about 10.9 ms to about 7.2 ms. A 128-thread block-size sweep validated but regressed, so final head reverts it and keeps 256 threads. Final NCU still shows the n=176 path is memory-throughput limited (~733 GB/s, low L2 hit), suggesting future work should reduce global matrix traffic rather than tune block size further; CUTE DSL remains unavailable so only load_inline CUDA was used.

Redesign only the n=176 path on d0eb40 to reduce global matrix traffic: stage Householder panel/column data in shared memory/registers and fuse read-modify-write updates across trailing columns where possible, preserving 256-thread warp reductions and all n32/rankdef/mixed dispatch behavior; profile current n176 first, then compare n176 speed/correctness before touching wider code.

Staged the active n=176 Householder vector in shared memory after normalization so trailing-column dot/update reuses vcol instead of rereading h0[:,k] from global memory; validation passed and benchmark improved to 93647.929 us, with n=176 down to ~6.27 ms.

Removed the per-trailing-column __syncthreads after n=176 update because the next block_sum provides the necessary barrier; validation passed and benchmark improved to 93425.792 us, with n=176 around 6.09 ms.

Best score reached 93425.792 us at f94119905af4d420296b4e17c3a16e5f609a0369, improving parent d0eb40 / 100060.115 us. The n=176 redesign stages the normalized Householder column in shared memory so dot/update loops reuse vcol instead of rereading h0[:,k] from global memory, then removes the redundant per-trailing-column barrier because the next block_sum synchronizes. Validation and guards passed; n=176 improved to about 6.09 ms. Final NCU still shows memory-throughput pressure (~736 GB/s, low L2 hit), so future gains likely require broader trailing-column tiling/fusing rather than more barrier/block tweaks. CUTE DSL remains unavailable; used executable load_inline CUDA.

Combine f941199 as base with only 6733ae's inline CUDA classifier changes for n512/n1024 rankdef/clustered masks/counts; preserve n176 staged-vcol/barrier behavior, n32, and mixed-split dispatch, validate the pure stack first, and compare active buckets (n176, n512, n1024, n32, mixed) before any follow-on edits.

Combined f941199 with only 6733ae's inline CUDA n512/n1024 structural classifier for rankdef/clustered masks and counts, preserving n176 staged-vcol/no-barrier, n32, and mixed split dispatch; validation passed and benchmark measured 93230.721 us.

Best score reached 93230.721 us at 268f2ec18c0071ef858d3bcb1b8d5993a039b768, slightly improving f941199 parent 93425.792 us. The brief was a pure combine: kept f941199's n176 staged-vcol/no-barrier kernel and n32 path, and added only 6733ae's inline CUDA structural classifier for n512/n1024 rankdef/clustered masks/counts feeding the existing mixed split dispatch. Validation and guards passed; active buckets stayed healthy with n176 about 6.09 ms and clustered n512 about 515 ms. Final profile of n512 clustered shows classifier/structural path is highly DRAM-bound, so future work should reduce classifier scan bandwidth or avoid scanning both rankdef and clustered tails when one is enough. CUTE DSL remains unavailable; used executable load_inline CUDA.

Further redesign n176 on 268f2ec: tile trailing-column Householder updates over small column blocks so each loaded/staged v/tau is reused across multiple columns with fewer global read/write passes; try warp-per-column or warp-group-per-column layouts while preserving staged vcol/no-barrier gains, warp reductions, n32, classifier, and mixed paths; keep only if n176 bucket and full geomean improve.

Tiled n=176 trailing Householder updates over four columns, reusing the staged vcol across four dot/update passes; validation passed and n176 improved to 5828.997 us, but full geomean regressed slightly to 93312.302 us versus parent 93230.721.

Expanded the n=176 trailing update tile from four to eight columns so each staged vcol load feeds eight column dot/update streams; validation passed, n176 improved to 5737.028 us, and full geomean improved to 93028.537 us versus parent 93230.721.

Retiled the n=176 trailing update to a 16-column local/scale array tile, reusing vcol across more columns with unrolled dot and update loops; validation passed and full geomean improved to 92905.162 us, best for this brief, with n176 about 5737.185 us.
Attempted to split n=176 16-column update tiles into predicate-free full tiles plus a predicated tail, but introduced a brace mismatch in the inline CUDA source; build failed before validation.

Fixed and validated the n=176 16-column tiling split: full tiles run predicate-free and only the final tail keeps bounds checks. This cut n176 to 4779.998 us and improved full geomean to 91791.435 us, the best brief result.

Best score reached 91791.435 us at ca6bd8c2c5a410b77a22d2e8dac39302e106ad86, improving parent 268f2ec / 93230.721 us. The successful n176 macro redesign tiles trailing Householder updates over 16 columns, then splits predicate-free full tiles from the predicated tail so each staged vcol load is reused across many columns without inner bounds checks; n176 dropped to about 4.78 ms. Four-column and eight-column tiles validated but were weaker; the full/tail split initially had a brace build_error that was logged and then fixed. Final NCU for n176 is saved and still shows memory throughput pressure (~733 GB/s, ~4.8% L2 hit), so future work could try a true multi-warp column-group layout or more aggressive row/column shared-memory blocking. CUTE DSL remained unavailable; used executable load_inline CUDA.

Combine ca6bd8's best n176 16-column predicate-free/tail-split tiling with fb0081's rankdef-first classifier short-circuit, using ca6bd8 as base and transplanting only classifier precedence/short-circuit changes; preserve n32, mixed split, dense fallback, and n176 full-tile behavior, then validate and benchmark the pure stack before any further edits.

Combined ca6bd8 n176 16-column predicate-free/tail-split tiling with fb0081 rankdef-first classifier short-circuit only. Validation passed and benchmark improved full geomean to 91341.981 us, preserving n32/mixed/dense fallback and n176 full-tile behavior.

Best score reached 91341.981 us at 87d8d1f33c732cdf0edff46fa432d2ede19690f4, improving ca6bd8 parent 91791.435 us. This was the requested pure combine: kept ca6bd8's n176 16-column predicate-free/tail-split kernel and transplanted only fb0081's rankdef-first classifier short-circuit so rankdef matrices skip the clustered scan; n32, mixed split, dense fallback, and n176 behavior were preserved. Validation and guards passed. Final rankdef NCU profile is saved; classifier path remains memory/L2-throughput heavy (~806 GB/s, ~98% L2 throughput), so future work should reduce structural scan traffic or specialize rankdef classification further. CUTE DSL remained unavailable, so executable load_inline CUDA was used.

Micro-tune only the n176 predicate-free/tail-split tiled update from 87d8: sweep tile width/register layout around the current 16-column local/scale arrays, test 24/32 columns only if ptxas occupancy/spills stay acceptable, and try smaller packed local storage to reduce register pressure; preserve classifier, n32, mixed, dense, and rankdef behavior; keep only if n176 bucket improves without geomean regression.

Swept n176 predicate-free/tail-split tile width from 16 to 24 columns with matching local/scale arrays. It built and validated, but n176 regressed to 4802.935 us and full geomean regressed to 91728.244 us versus parent 91341.981, suggesting register pressure/tail shape outweighs reuse.

Swept n176 tile width from 24 to 32 columns. It built and validated, with full geomean 91212.206 us, but n176 regressed to 4958.877 us versus the 16-column parent and the geomean gain came from unrelated noisy large shapes, so it does not satisfy the n176-bucket objective.

Restored 16-column tile width but reused local[] in-place for scale values to remove the separate scale[16] array. It built and validated, but n176 regressed to 4789.501 us and full geomean regressed to 91634.944 us, so the original separate scale array remains better.

Restored the parent 16-column n176 predicate-free/tail-split tile with separate local[16]/scale[16] arrays after 24-column, 32-column, and in-place-scale variants all regressed the n176 bucket. No new benchmark was run for the exact restore; carrying forward the parent metric 91341.981 us for final head.

Measured the restored parent 16-column n176 tile after build and full validation. Benchmark produced n176 4780.483 us and full geomean 91714.669 us, confirming no tested micro-tune beat the original n176 layout in this brief.
